sites.rationale: L13 reports N-terminal FLAG on hMRAP1a (human MRAP isoform a, this protein), grounding an N-terminal extracellular tag. Because no residue is named and there is no signal peptide, the only unambiguous junction is insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before Met-1). This is a distinct junction from the L2 site (insert_after=1, after Met). The extracellular N-terminus spans residues 1–37, 37 residues from the TM boundary, so steric clearance is ample. Ranked below L2 because no functional or surface-detection assay is reported. Full-length human hMRAP1a and hMRAP1b were commercially synthesized with an N-terminal FLAG tag for transfection experiments (L13). No residue number is stated; the N-terminus (residue 1, Met) is extracellular per the canonical topology (residues 1–37 extracellular, no signal peptide), so the tag prepends before Met-1.

sources.claim: N-terminal myc-tagged hMC3R and N-terminal Flag-tagged hMRAP1a, hMRAP1b, hMRAP2a, hMRAP2b, and hMRAP2c were commercially synthesized by Synbio Technologies (Monmouth Junction, NJ, USA) to generate the plasmids used for transfection.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: ACTH-stimulated cAMP reporter assay in mammalian cells: AP–MRAP supported cAMP responses comparable to unmodified MRAP (Figure 1B of PMC4947873). Function fully preserved.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly states the AP tag was placed 'immediately after the initiating Met' of full-length mMRAP, pinning the junction to insert_after_residue=1 (M→A). The canonical human MRAP sequence has Met at position 1 and Ala at position 2, matching exactly. The extracellular span is residues 1–37 (37 residues to TM boundary at 38), giving ample clearance. L6 confirms functional equivalence to unmodified MRAP in a cAMP assay, making this the highest-confidence surface site. Full-length mMRAP expressed in mammalian cells with the 15-aa AP sequence (GLNDIFEAQKIEWHE) inserted immediately after the initiating Met (residue 1), yielding AP–MRAP. Selective biotinylation with ER-targeted or cytoplasmic biotin ligase confirmed extracellular display of the N-terminal tag. Construct also combined with C-terminal V5–3xFLAG.

sources.claim: AP–MRAP contained the minimal AP sequence GLNDIFEAQKIEWHE immediately after the initiating Met followed by mMRAP or mMRAP–V5–3xFlag.

literature_notes: MRAP is a single-pass type I membrane protein with a well-documented dual topology (N-out/C-in and N-in/C-out), confirmed by BiFC (L9) and biotin-ligase accessibility (L4–L6). The canonical topology provided places residues 1–37 extracellular, TM at 38–60, and residues 61–172 intracellular. All C-terminal tags (L1, L3, L7, L8) are therefore intracellular in the canonical orientation and are recorded in other_positions. L9 (YFP BiFC at both termini) and L10 (MRAP2 ortholog with N- and C-terminal FLAG detected on intact-cell surface) further confirm dual topology but do not change the canonical-topology classification used here. L5 mentions a Flag epitope in the AP–MRAP constructs but does not specify its position independently of L2/L3, so it adds no new site. L11 and L12 report MRAP2 C-terminal FLAG by western blot only (no surface detection), providing no additional surface sites for MRAP.

literature_other_positions.note: V5–3xFLAG appended to the C-terminus of full-length mMRAP; residue 172 (S) lies within the intracellular span (61–172) of the canonical topology.
AP sequence appended to the C-terminus of full-length mMRAP (MRAP–AP); C-terminus is intracellular in canonical topology, confirmed by cytoplasmic biotin-ligase biotinylation.
3xFLAG appended to the C-terminus of full-length human MRAPα via p3xFLAG-CMV-14 vector; C-terminus is intracellular in canonical topology.
FLAG appended to the C-terminus of full-length human MRAPα (MRAP-FLAG); detected by immunofluorescence in permeabilized CHO cells, consistent with intracellular localisation in canonical topology.
